Masashi Kishimoto: Masashi Kishimoto created Naruto, which ran in Weekly Shonen Jump from 1999 to 2014 and became one of the best-selling manga of all time. He later supervised and briefly wrote Boruto: Naruto Next Generations and created the one-shot sci-fi series Samurai 8.
Tsugumi Ohba: Tsugumi Ohba is the pen name of the writer behind Death Note, Bakuman and Platinum End, all drawn by artist Takeshi Obata. Ohba is known for tense, clever plots built around games of wits.
CLAMP: CLAMP is an all-women team of manga creators formed in the late 1980s. Their many hits include Cardcaptor Sakura, Magic Knight Rayearth, Chobits, xxxHolic and Tsubasa: Reservoir Chronicle, and their series often cross over with one another.
Atsushi Ohkubo: Atsushi Ohkubo created Soul Eater, the gothic action series about a weapon school, and its follow-up universe series Fire Force. Both were adapted into popular anime.
Yuu Watase: Yuu Watase is a beloved shojo artist best known for Fushigi Yugi, Ceres: Celestial Legend, Imadoki!, Alice 19th and Absolute Boyfriend. Her stories mix romance with fantasy and adventure.
Fujino Omori: Fujino Omori writes the light novel series Is It Wrong to Try to Pick Up Girls in a Dungeon? (DanMachi) and its spin-offs such as Sword Oratoria, which have been adapted into manga and anime.
Tetsuya Nomura: Tetsuya Nomura is the Square Enix designer and director who created the Kingdom Hearts games. The Kingdom Hearts manga adaptations were drawn by Shiro Amano.
Bisco Hatori: Bisco Hatori created the hit romantic comedy Ouran High School Host Club. Her earlier series Millennium Snow is a gentle vampire romance.
Yoshitoki Oima: Yoshitoki Oima wrote and drew A Silent Voice, a moving story about bullying and redemption that became an acclaimed anime film, and the ongoing epic To Your Eternity.
Kohei Horikoshi: Kohei Horikoshi created My Hero Academia, the superhero school series that ran in Weekly Shonen Jump from 2014 to 2024 and became a worldwide hit with its anime.
Peach-Pit: Peach-Pit is the duo of Banri Sendo and Shibuko Ebara, creators of Shugo Chara!, Rozen Maiden, DearS and Zombie-Loan.
Shuzo Oshimi: Shuzo Oshimi writes intense psychological manga such as The Flowers of Evil, Inside Mari, Happiness and Blood on the Tracks, known for their unsettling, deeply human characters.
Norio Sakurai: Norio Sakurai created The Dangers in My Heart, a sweet and funny middle-school romance that was adapted into anime, and I Think I Turned My Childhood Friend into a Girl.
Haruichi Furudate: Haruichi Furudate created Haikyu!!, the volleyball series that ran in Weekly Shonen Jump from 2012 to 2020 and helped launch a volleyball boom in Japan.
Tomohito Oda: Tomohito Oda created Komi Can't Communicate, a gentle comedy about a girl with severe social anxiety trying to make 100 friends.
AidaIro: AidaIro is the creator of Toilet-bound Hanako-kun, a stylish supernatural series about school ghost stories, adapted into anime in 2020.
ONE and Yusuke Murata: One-Punch Man began as a webcomic by ONE (also the creator of Mob Psycho 100) and was redrawn by Yusuke Murata, the artist of Eyeshield 21, into one of the best-looking action manga around.
Gege Akutami: Gege Akutami created Jujutsu Kaisen, the dark supernatural action series that ran in Weekly Shonen Jump from 2018 to 2024, along with its prequel Jujutsu Kaisen 0.
Koyoharu Gotouge: Koyoharu Gotouge created Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba, which ran from 2016 to 2020 and became one of the best-selling manga ever after its anime adaptation.
Tatsuya Endo: Tatsuya Endo created Spy x Family, the action-comedy about a spy, an assassin and a telepathic girl pretending to be a family.
Yana Toboso: Yana Toboso created Black Butler, the gothic mystery about a demon butler in Victorian England, and wrote the story for Twisted-Wonderland.
Tite Kubo: Tite Kubo created Bleach, which ran in Weekly Shonen Jump from 2001 to 2016, and the one-shot follow-up world of Burn the Witch.
Sui Ishida: Sui Ishida created Tokyo Ghoul and its sequel Tokyo Ghoul:re, dark fantasy horror about a college student who becomes half-ghoul.
Tatsuki Fujimoto: Tatsuki Fujimoto created Chainsaw Man and Fire Punch, plus acclaimed one-shots like Look Back and Goodbye, Eri.
Riichiro Inagaki and Boichi: Dr. Stone is written by Riichiro Inagaki (Eyeshield 21) and drawn by Korean artist Boichi, known for his incredibly detailed art.
Kazue Kato: Kazue Kato created Blue Exorcist, the dark fantasy series about the son of Satan training to become an exorcist.
Hajime Isayama: Hajime Isayama created Attack on Titan, which ran from 2009 to 2021 and became a global phenomenon.
Nobuhiro Watsuki: Nobuhiro Watsuki created Rurouni Kenshin, the Meiji-era samurai series, as well as Busou Renkin and Embalming.
Yuna Kagesaki: Yuna Kagesaki created Chibi Vampire (Karin), the comedy about a vampire girl who has too much blood instead of too little.
Negi Haruba: Negi Haruba created The Quintessential Quintuplets, the romantic comedy about a tutor and five identical sisters.
Kafka Asagiri: Kafka Asagiri writes Bungo Stray Dogs, drawn by Sango Harukawa, in which famous literary authors become gifted detectives and villains.
Kouta Hirano: Kouta Hirano created Hellsing, the over-the-top vampire action series, and Drifters.
Yoshihiro Togashi: Yoshihiro Togashi created YuYu Hakusho and Hunter x Hunter, two of the most influential shonen action series.
Naoya Matsumoto: Naoya Matsumoto created Kaiju No. 8, the hit series about a man who becomes a monster while trying to join the team that fights them.
Rumiko Takahashi: Rumiko Takahashi is one of the best-selling manga artists ever, creator of Urusei Yatsura, Maison Ikkoku, Ranma 1/2, InuYasha and Mao.
Hiromu Arakawa: Hiromu Arakawa created Fullmetal Alchemist, the alchemy adventure about the Elric brothers, and Silver Spoon, inspired by her farm upbringing.
Hiro Mashima: Hiro Mashima created Rave Master, Fairy Tail and Edens Zero, energetic fantasy adventures full of friendship and magic.
Eiichiro Oda: Eiichiro Oda created One Piece, the pirate adventure running since 1997 and the best-selling manga series of all time.
Natsuki Takaya: Natsuki Takaya created Fruits Basket, the beloved shojo story about a family cursed to turn into zodiac animals, and Twinkle Stars.
Ken Akamatsu: Ken Akamatsu created the romantic comedies Love Hina and Negima! Magister Negi Magi, and its sequel UQ Holder!.
Arina Tanemura: Arina Tanemura is a shojo artist known for Full Moon o Sagashite, Phantom Thief Jeanne and The Gentlemen's Alliance.
Matsuri Hino: Matsuri Hino created the gothic romance Vampire Knight and the fairy-tale comedy MeruPuri.
Kentaro Yabuki: Kentaro Yabuki created Black Cat and drew the To Love Ru series and Ayakashi Triangle.
Mizuho Kusanagi: Mizuho Kusanagi created Yona of the Dawn, the fantasy epic about a princess who becomes a warrior.
Nakaba Suzuki: Nakaba Suzuki created The Seven Deadly Sins and its sequel Four Knights of the Apocalypse.
Hiroyuki Takei: Hiroyuki Takei created Shaman King, the supernatural tournament series about shamans who team up with spirits.
Julietta Suzuki: Julietta Suzuki created Kamisama Kiss, the shojo romance about a girl who becomes a land god with a fox-spirit familiar.
Aka Akasaka: Aka Akasaka created the romantic comedy Kaguya-sama: Love Is War and writes Oshi no Ko.
Kaiu Shirai: Kaiu Shirai wrote The Promised Neverland, drawn by Posuka Demizu, the thriller about orphans who discover the dark truth of their home.
Yusei Matsui: Yusei Matsui created Assassination Classroom and Neuro: Supernatural Detective.
Kore Yamazaki: Kore Yamazaki created The Ancient Magus' Bride, a fantasy about a girl apprenticed to a mysterious inhuman mage.
Nagabe: Nagabe created The Girl from the Other Side: Siúil, a Rún, a quiet, fairy-tale-like story told in striking black and white.
